title: Distribution and richness of Orthohantavirus reservoir hosts: Implications for zoonotic risk in Southern South America.

analysis.background: Orthohantaviruses represent a major zoonotic threat in Southern South America, with 13 native rodent species recognized as reservoirs of 15 viral genotypes, and existing distribution information is fragmented, limiting risk assessment.
analysis.methods: The authors compiled and curated occurrence records for reservoir hosts, used ecological niche modeling to estimate potential distributions, integrated binary presence predictions to map reservoir and genotype richness, and combined richness maps with gridded human population data to estimate the number of people potentially exposed.
analysis.results: Most reservoir species are predicted across eastern and northeastern Argentina, parts of Paraguay, Uruguay, and southern Brazil; hotspots of reservoir richness are concentrated in the Humid Chaco, while high genotype richness extends across the Chaco‑Pampean plain; exposure to ≥7 pathogenic genotypes is estimated to exceed 13 million people under the most precautionary scenario.
analysis.contribution: This study provides the first integrated, region‑wide assessment of Orthohantavirus reservoir distributions and richness in Southern South America, offering an updated ecological baseline to support surveillance, risk mapping, and prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations: Only the abstract is available; detailed methods, validation, sample sizes, and uncertainty estimates are not reported.

title: Differentiating Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) andHemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS) Using a Stacking Ensemble

title: Distribution and richness of Orthohantavirus reservoir hosts: Implications for zoonotic risk in Southern South America.

analysis.background: Orthohantaviruses represent a major zoonotic threat in Southern South America, with 13 native rodent species identified as reservoirs of 15 viral genotypes, and fragmented distribution information limits regional exposure risk assessment.
analysis.methods: The authors compiled occurrence records for reservoir hosts, applied ecological niche modeling to estimate potential distributions, integrated binary presence predictions to map reservoir and genotype richness, and combined richness maps with gridded human population data to estimate numbers of potentially exposed people.

analysis.contribution: The study provides the first integrated, region‑wide assessment of Orthohantavirus reservoir distributions and richness in Southern South America, offering an updated ecological baseline to support surveillance, risk mapping, and prevention strategies.

title: Distribution and richness of Orthohantavirus reservoir hosts: Implications for zoonotic risk in Southern South America.

analysis.background: Orthohantaviruses are a major zoonotic threat in Southern South America, with 13 native rodent species serving as reservoirs for 15 viral genotypes, and existing distribution data are fragmented, hindering risk assessment.
analysis.methods: The authors compiled and curated occurrence records for reservoir hosts in the region, applied ecological niche modeling to predict potential distributions, integrated binary presence predictions to map reservoir and genotype richness, and overlaid these maps with gridded human population data to estimate exposure.

analysis.contribution: This work delivers the first region‑wide integrated assessment of Orthohantavirus reservoir distributions and richness, providing an ecological baseline for surveillance, risk mapping, and prevention strategies in Southern South America.

title: Differentiating Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) andHemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS) Using a Stacking Ensemble

analysis.background: Distinguishing Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) from Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS) is challenging once organ‑specific symptoms appear, delaying timely clinical decisions.
analysis.methods: The study generated 8,000 synthetic records with 22 symptom features, applied binary encoding and SMOTE within 5‑fold stratified cross‑validation, and trained a stacking ensemble of XGBoost and LightGBM base learners with Logistic Regression as the meta‑learner.

analysis.contribution: The framework demonstrates methodological potential for differentiating HPS and HFRS using symptom data and provides a basis for future validation with prospective clinical datasets.
analysis.limitations: The model was trained on synthetic data, and no publicly available structured HPS/HFRS symptom dataset exists, limiting real‑world applicability.

title: Ecological Cascades and Future Hantavirus Spillover Risk in a Changing Climate

analysis.background: Anthropogenic climate change is reshaping biodiversity and accelerating zoonotic spillover, with rodent-borne orthohantaviruses causing severe human diseases. The 2026 Andes virus cruise ship outbreak underscores the globalized threat, yet macroecological synthesis linking environmental drivers to hantavirus risks remains lacking.
analysis.methods: An integrated ecological and machine learning framework combines 89 virus-host associations across 61 reservoir species with mechanistic Force-of-Infection (FOI) modeling to project spillover hazards under climate scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5) for 2041–2060.
analysis.results: Models predict a 74.9% increase in FOI across modeled land area, with three high-hazard belts in temperate regions. Transmission dynamics vary by virus: thermal/precipitation anomalies drive Old/New World lineages, while urban-centric profiles emerge for Seoul and Mamore viruses due to anthropogenic landscape changes.
analysis.contribution: The study provides a baseline for global surveillance and emphasizes integrating spatial conservation with public health planning to address climate-driven spillover restructuring.
analysis.limitations: The paper is a preprint with partial text; specific host population data, sample sizes, or geographic locations are not reported. Causal relationships between climate variables and spillover are inferred from associations.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Climate change accelerates hantavirus spillover, but macroecological links remain unexplored. Methods: FOI modeling with 89 virus-host associations projects spillover under climate scenarios. Results: 74.9% of land area shows increased FOI, with distinct high-risk regions and virus-specific drivers. Contribution: Maps guide surveillance and highlight conservation-health integration. Limitations: Preprint with partial data; causal inferences lack direct evidence.

title: IMMUNOINFORMATICS-GUIDED MULTI-EPITOPE VACCINE CANDIDATE DESIGN AND MHC DOCKING VALIDATION TARGETING THE GLYCOPROTEIN PRECURSOR OF THE NEWLY REPORTED ANDV/Switzerland/Hu-3337/2026 ORTHOHANTAVIRUS

analysis.background: The rapid release of viral genomic sequences enables early immunoinformatics screening for vaccine design. This study addresses the need for rapid vaccine development against newly emerging orthohantaviruses.
analysis.methods: The glycoprotein precursor (GP) of ANDV/Switzerland/Hu-3337/2026 was analyzed using antigenicity prediction (VaxiJen), conserved-region screening, transmembrane topology analysis, MHC-I/II epitope prediction, and molecular docking against MHC receptors.

analysis.contribution: This computational workflow prioritizes multi-epitope vaccine candidates for ANDV/Switzerland/Hu-3337/2026, accelerating preclinical vaccine design and enabling rapid response to emerging orthohantaviruses.
analysis.limitations: The study is based solely on in silico analysis; experimental validation, population coverage assessment, and allergenicity/toxicity testing are required for clinical translation.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Rapid vaccine design is critical for emerging orthohantaviruses. Methods: In silico analysis of ANDV/Switzerland/Hu-3337/2026 GP included antigenicity prediction, epitope selection, and MHC docking. analysis.background: BACKGROUND: Andes virus (ANDV) is the only hantavirus known to transmit between humans and causes hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in Chile and Argentina.
analysis.methods: In Chile, ANDV genomic diversity remains incompletely characterised.
analysis.results: This study aimed to characterise the genetic diversity, geographical structure, and molecular signatures of ANDV using human clinical samples collected over a 13-year period (2011-24). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective genomic epidemiology study of ANDV infections in Chile.
analysis.contribution: Clinical samples from patients with confirmed ANDV, collected between March 9, 2011, and June 27, 2024, were analysed and sequenced.

title: Can hantaviruses cause pandemics?

analysis.background: Abstract The 2026 MV Hondius outbreak of Andes virus (ANDV) renewed concerns regarding the pandemic potential of hantaviruses, particularly because ANDV is the only hantavirus with proved human-to-human transmission.
analysis.main_directions: These concerns and fears are justified by the profound negative impact of the recent COVID-19 pandemic. Hantaviruses are segmented negative-sense RNA viruses maintained mainly in rodents and transmitted to man primarily through inhalation of contaminated aerosols.
analysis.current_state: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome predominates in Europe and Asia, whereas hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome occurs in North and South Americas and carries high mortality.
analysis.gaps: 当前仅依据已获得的摘要或正文片段，未进行超出证据的推断。
analysis.future_research: Although most hantaviruses have no human-to-human transmissibility, ANDV outbreaks demonstrate that transmission between humans is possible under close-contact conditions.

analysis.background: Background In Chile, Andes virus (ANDV) is the sole aetiological agent of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) with mean annual incidence of 55 cases, 32% case fatality rate (CFR) and no specific treatment.
analysis.methods: Neutralizing antibody (NAb) titres at hospital admission correlate inversely with HCPS severity.
analysis.results: We designed an open trial to explore safety and efficacy and evaluate pharmacokinetics of immune plasma as a treatment strategy for this disease. title: Cytokine expression during early and late phase of acute Puumala hantavirus infection

analysis.background: Abstract Background Hantaviruses of the family Bunyaviridae are emerging zoonotic pathogens which cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in the Old World and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in the New World.

analysis.results: The aim of our study was to investigate cytokine expression during the course of acute Puumala hantavirus infection. Results We retrospectively studied 64 patients hospitalised with acute Puumala hantavirus infection in 2010 during a hantavirus epidemic in Germany.

title: Ribavirin Protects Syrian Hamsters against Lethal Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome — After Intranasal Exposure to Andes Virus

analysis.background: Andes virus, ANDV, harbored by wild rodents, causes the highly lethal hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) upon transmission to humans resulting in death in 30% to 50% of the cases.
analysis.methods: As there is no treatment for this disease, we systematically tested the efficacy of ribavirin in vitro and in an animal model.
analysis.results: In vitro assays confirmed antiviral activity and determined that the most effective doses were 40 μg/mL and above. We tested three different concentrations of ribavirin for their capability to prevent HPS in the ANDV hamster model following an intranasal challenge.
analysis.contribution: While the highest level of ribavirin (200 mg/kg) was toxic to the hamster, both the middle (100 mg/kg) and the lowest concentration (50 mg/kg) prevented HPS in hamsters without toxicity.

title: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome: 1993–2018

analysis.background: OBJECTIVES From 1993 to 2018, hantavirus infections were reported in 39 states, with hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) as the most common and fatal manifestation.
analysis.methods: To identify differences in the presentation of HPS between children and adults, we hypothesized that children with HPS would be diagnosed later in their illness course given the nonspecific clinical features of HPS.
analysis.results: METHODS This was an evaluation of the clinical and demographic characteristics of national HPS cases from 1993 to 2018. Data were from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention database and 1 state department of health, comprising 97% of US cases.
analysis.contribution: We compared children (0 to 12 years), adolescents (13 to 18 years), and adults using nonparametric and parametric analyses, with additional exploratory analyses to identify clinical variables associated with mortality.

title: Coagulopathy in Acute Puumala Hantavirus Infection

analysis.background: Puumala hantavirus (PUUV) causes a hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), also called nephropathia epidemica (NE), which is mainly endemic in Europe and Russia.
analysis.methods: The clinical features include a low platelet count, altered coagulation, endothelial activation, and acute kidney injury (AKI).
analysis.results: Multiple connections between coagulation pathways and inflammatory mediators, as well as complement and kallikrein–kinin systems, have been reported. The bleeding symptoms are usually mild.
analysis.contribution: PUUV-infected patients also have an increased risk for disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and thrombosis.

title: Hantaan Virus Infection Causes an Acute Neurological Disease That Is Fatal in Adult Laboratory Mice

analysis.background: ABSTRACT Hantaan virus, the etiological agent of Korean hemorrhagic fever, is transmitted to humans from persistently infected mice ( Apodemus agrarius ), which serve as the primary reservoir.
analysis.methods: Here we demonstrate that several strains of adult Mus musculus domesticus (C57BL/6, BALB/c, AKR/J, and SJL/J) were susceptible to Hantaan virus infection when infected intraperitoneally.
analysis.results: First clinical signs were loss of weight, ruffled fur, and reduced activity, which were followed by neurological symptoms, such as paralyses and convulsions. Within 2 days of disease onset, the animals died of acute encephalitis.
analysis.contribution: PCR analysis indicated a systemic infection with viral RNA present in all major organs.

title: Central Nervous System and Ocular Manifestations in Puumala Hantavirus Infection

analysis.background: Puumala hantavirus (PUUV), carried and spread by the bank vole (Myodes glareolus), causes a mild form of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) called nephropathia epidemica (NE).
analysis.main_directions: Acute high fever, acute kidney injury (AKI), thrombocytopenia, and hematuria are typical features of this syndrome. In addition, headache, blurred vision, insomnia, vertigo, and nausea are commonly associated with the disease.
analysis.current_state: This review explores the mechanisms and presentations of ocular and central nervous system involvement in acute NE.

title: Beyond ECMO Survival: Long-Term Symptom Burden and Quality-of-Life Impairment in Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome Survivors

analysis.background: Andes virus (ANDV) is the leading cause of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) in South America, a severe zoonosis with high mortality.
analysis.methods: Advances in critical care and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) have significantly improved survival rates;
analysis.results: however, data on recovery beyond survival remain limited. This multicenter cohort study enrolled laboratory-confirmed HCPS survivors in Chile between 2021 and 2024, with follow-up at 3–6 months post-symptom onset to assess physical and neuropsychological sequelae.
analysis.contribution: Participants were stratified by ECMO requirement and the clinical severity of HCPS, and evaluated using self-reported recovery, standardized symptom questionnaires, and EQ-5D quality-of-life instruments.

title: Ribavirin post-exposure prophylaxis for Andes virus exposure: a viewpoint.

analysis.scope_and_question: Andes virus (ANDV) is unique among hantaviruses because person-to-person transmission is possible.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This raises questions on the relevance of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), particularly following high-risk household, healthcare-associated, or laboratory exposures, considering its high case fatality rate.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Ribavirin has demonstrated antiviral activity against hantaviruses in vitro and in animal models, although clinical evidence supporting its use for ANDV remains extremely limited. This viewpoint summarises the currently available evidence regarding ribavirin as PEP after potential ANDV exposure. We discuss the knowledge gaps that may limit the applicability of ribavirin PEP, to make informed decisions on the use of ribavirin in the setting of PEP.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Potential dosing strategies are visualised by modelling and simulation, and potential dose and duration are discussed.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Although the biological rationale for ribavirin PEP appears compelling, absence of controlled human studies and potential toxicity currently limit its role to highly selected exposure scenarios and use shortly after exposure.

title: Can hantaviruses cause pandemics?

analysis.scope_and_question: Abstract The 2026 MV Hondius outbreak of Andes virus (ANDV) renewed concerns regarding the pandemic potential of hantaviruses, particularly because ANDV is the only hantavirus with proved human-to-human transmission.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: These concerns and fears are justified by the profound negative impact of the recent COVID-19 pandemic.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Hantaviruses are segmented negative-sense RNA viruses maintained mainly in rodents and transmitted to man primarily through inhalation of contaminated aerosols. Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome predominates in Europe and Asia, whereas hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome occurs in North and South Americas and carries high mortality. Although most hantaviruses have no human-to-human transmissibility, ANDV outbreaks demonstrate that transmission between humans is possible under close-contact conditions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Comparison with previous pandemics and WHO priority pathogens highlights several pandemic-associated features shared by hantaviruses, including zoonotic origin, RNA genome variability, and environmental influences.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: In this review, we will try to find the answer for the question “Can hantaviruses cause the next pandemic?”.

analysis.summary_en: Abstract The 2026 MV Hondius outbreak of Andes virus (ANDV) renewed concerns regarding the pandemic potential of hantaviruses, particularly because ANDV is the only hantavirus with proved human-to-human transmission. These concerns and fears are justified by the profound negative impact of the recent COVID-19 pandemic. Hantaviruses are segmented negative-sense RNA viruses maintained mainly in rodents and transmitted to man primarily through inhalation of contaminated aerosols. Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome predominates in Europe and Asia, whereas hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome occurs in North and South Americas and carries high mortality. Although most hantaviruses have no human-to-human transmissibility, ANDV outbreaks demonstrate that transmission between humans is possible under close-contact conditions. Comparison with previous pandemics and WHO priority pathogens highlights several pandemic-associated features shared by hantaviruses, including zoonotic origin, RNA genome variability, and environmental influences. In this review, we will try to find the answer for the question “Can hantaviruses cause the next pandemic?”.
